x: The module list covers about 190 GW, while the cell list covers only about 25 GW.

s: What does ALMM List-II cover?
x: ALMM List-I covers modules, List-II cells and List-III ingots and wafers.

s: On 22 September 2025, GST on solar devices was cut from 12% to what rate?
x: GST on solar devices was cut from 12% to 5%.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's solar manufacturing rules:
1. Domestic cells/modules are compulsory in CPSU, PM-KUSUM and rooftop-subsidy projects.
2. From April 2022, Basic Customs Duty is 40% on cells and 25% on modules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: DCR makes domestic cells/modules compulsory in those projects; BCD is 40% on modules and 25% on cells, not the reverse.

s: When was the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission ('Solar India') launched?
x: The mission was launched in January 2010 as one of NAPCC's eight missions; June 2015 is when its target was revised to 100 GW.

s: When the National Solar Mission target was revised to 100 GW by 2022 in June 2015, what was the rooftop solar component?
x: The revised target of June 2015 was 100 GW by 2022: 40 GW rooftop and 60 GW large/medium grid-connected projects.

s: Which National Solar Mission phase–period pair is correctly matched?
x: Phase III covered 2017–2022; Phase I was 2010–2013 and Phase II 2014–2017.

s: What is the successor long-term goal of India's solar-energy transition?
x: India’s successor goal is 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030, associated with its COP26 pledge.

s: The National Solar Mission is one of how many missions under the NAPCC (2008)?
x: NSM ('Solar India') is one of the 8 missions of the National Action Plan on Climate Change.

s: What was the off-grid PV target of Phase I (2010-2013) of the National Solar Mission?
x: Phase I aimed at 200 MW off-grid PV; Phase II 1,000 MW and Phase III 2,000 MW.

s: What does the National Solar Mission aim to make India?
o: Free of all thermal power by 2022
A global leader in solar energy
x: NSM aims to promote solar power and make India a global leader in solar energy.

s: What was the original target of grid-connected solar power by 2022 under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission?
x: The original target was 20 GW; it was raised to 100 GW in June 2015.

s: Where is the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE), an autonomous body of MNRE, located?
x: NISE is at Gurugram and is the technical focal point for solar R&D.

s: How much solar irradiation per square metre per day do most parts of India receive?
x: Most of India receives 4–7 kWh/m²/day, with 250–300 clear sunny days a year.

s: At how much has NISE estimated India's ground-based solar potential, assuming use of 3% of wasteland?
x: NISE estimates about 748 GW, of which only about 4.5% has been used.

s: Which State has the largest share of India's estimated renewable-energy potential, at about 23.70 per cent?
x: Rajasthan leads with about 23.70%. Maharashtra follows with 14.26%, while Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh each have about 9.10%.

s: India receives about how many clear sunny days a year?
x: India gets 250-300 clear sunny days a year, which gives it huge solar potential.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's share of India's estimated renewable-energy potential?
x: AP has about 9.10%; Rajasthan 23.70%, Maharashtra 14.26% and Karnataka 8.59%.

s: Under PM-KUSUM, solar pumps are covered by which components?
x: Component B covers standalone solar pumps and C solarises grid-connected pumps; A is for small grid-connected plants.

s: Which body regulates the Indian Energy Exchange (IEX), established in 2008?
x: IEX is regulated by CERC and trades DAM, TAM, renewable energy and ESCerts.

s: To what capacity was the target of the Solar Park Scheme enhanced on 21 March 2017?
x: Launched on 12 December 2014 with a 20 GW target for over 25 parks, the scheme was raised to 40 GW on 21 March 2017.

s: With which scheme are rooftop solar incentives, the ARUN app and Suryamitra skilling associated?
x: SRISTI is associated with rooftop incentives, the ARUN app and Suryamitra skill development.

s: To what level did the Green Energy Open Access Rules, 2022 cut the open-access threshold for green power from 1 MW?
x: The Ministry of Power's Rules cut the threshold from 1 MW to 100 kW.

s: The PM Surya Sarovar Yojana (₹5,070 crore) targets how much floating solar capacity by 2030–31?
x: The scheme involves ₹5,070 crore and targets 5,000 MW of floating solar by 2030–31.

s: Under the PM Surya Sarovar Yojana, Central Financial Assistance of up to how much is provided, and through which agency is the scheme implemented?
o: Rs 1 crore per MW, through SECI
Rs 10 lakh per MW, through NISE
Rs 1 crore per MW, through IREDA
Rs 5 crore per MW, through NTPC
x: The scheme gives CFA of up to Rs 1 crore/MW and the 5,000 MW target is to be delivered via SECI. NISE did the floating-potential assessment, IREDA and NTPC are not the stated agency, and Rs 10 lakh or Rs 5 crore per MW are wrong amounts.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana?
o: It provides free power up to 500 units per month
It is a Central Sector scheme for 2024 to 2026-27
It aims to cover one crore rooftop households
It envisages 30 GW of rooftop solar capacity
x: The scheme provides free power up to 300 units per month, not 500.

s: What does Component B of PM-KUSUM cover?
o: Small grid-connected plants on barren land or farmland
x: Component B covers standalone solar pumps; A covers small grid-connected plants and C solarisation of grid-connected pumps.

s: What is the outlay of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana?
x: The scheme, launched in February 2024, has an outlay of about Rs 75,021 crore.

s: Which scheme–purpose pair is correctly matched?
o: VGF schemes – viability gap funding for grid-scale solar developers
PM-KUSUM Component C – standalone solar pumps
PM-KUSUM Component B – solarisation of grid-connected pumps
Rooftop Solar Phase-II – floating solar generation
x: VGF schemes, including JNNSM Phase-II through SECI, fund grid-scale solar developers; Component B is standalone pumps and Component C grid-connected pump solarisation.

s: Which power is traded in the Green Term Ahead Market (GTAM), launched in 2020 on the Indian Energy Exchange?
x: GTAM is a renewable-energy-only trading segment on the IEX, launched in 2020.

s: When was the Solar Park Scheme launched?
x: The Solar Park Scheme began on 12 December 2014; its target was raised to 40 GW on 21 March 2017.

s: Through which agency are viability gap funding (VGF) schemes for grid-scale solar developers under JNNSM Phase-II implemented?
x: VGF schemes run through SECI; NEDCAP is AP's nodal agency and NISE an R&D body.

s: What must government producers use to set up solar plants under the CPSU Scheme Phase-II (2019)?
x: CPSU Phase-II gives VGF to government producers using domestic cells and modules.

s:
Arrange the following solar schemes in chronological order of launch:
1. PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
2. Solar Park Scheme
3. National Solar Mission
4. PM Surya Sarovar Yojana
x: NSM (Jan 2010), Solar Park Scheme (Dec 2014), PM Surya Ghar (Feb 2024), PM Surya Sarovar (Jul 2026).

s: Under PM Surya Ghar's Model Solar Village component, to whom is ₹1 crore given?
x: Model Solar Village gives ₹1 crore to one village in each district.

s: In which year was the PLI scheme for High-Efficiency Solar PV Modules launched?
x: PLI for high-efficiency modules came in 2021; ALMM became compulsory in 2019.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Kurnool Solar Park has a stated capacity of 1,000 MW. Pavagada, not Kurnool, has a capacity of 2,050 MW.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Khavda Renewable Energy Park — Kutch, Gujarat
Omkareshwar Floating Solar Park — Jodhpur, Rajasthan
Bhadla Solar Park — Khandwa, Madhya Pradesh
Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park — Kutch, Gujarat
x: Khavda Renewable Energy Park is located in Kutch, Gujarat. Omkareshwar is in Khandwa, Madhya Pradesh, Bhadla is in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, and Kurnool is in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which of the following is NOT identified as one of the three ultra mega solar parks in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Kurnool, NP Kunta and Kadapa are the three Andhra Pradesh ultra mega solar park locations. Omkareshwar is associated with the largest floating solar plant.

s: Ramagiri in Ananthapuramu district of Andhra Pradesh is known for which type of renewable-energy park?
o: Ultra mega solar park of 2,245 MW
x: Ramagiri hosts a hybrid solar-wind park. AP's floating plant is NTPC Simhadri; AP has no geothermal park of this kind; the 2,245 MW park is Bhadla in Rajasthan.

s: Bhadla, the largest commissioned solar park (2,245 MW), is in which State?
x: Bhadla is in Jodhpur, Rajasthan; Pavagada is in Karnataka and Kurnool in AP.

s: Which renewable-energy park in Kutch, Gujarat will be the world's largest when complete?
x: Khavda RE Park (~30 GW solar-wind) in Kutch will be the world's largest RE park.

s: Under the AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy push (April 2026), how much barren land was offered for solar lease?
x: AP offered 50,000 acres of barren land for solar lease in April 2026.

s: In which State is the Pavagada solar park (2,050 MW) located?
x: Pavagada (2,050 MW) is in Karnataka; Bhadla in Rajasthan is the largest commissioned park.

s: In which district of Rajasthan is the Bhadla solar park located?
x: Bhadla solar park (2,245 MW), the largest commissioned, is in Jodhpur district, Rajasthan.

s: Which State leads India's floating solar potential on reservoirs, with about 16 GW?
x: Maharashtra (about 16 GW) and Madhya Pradesh (about 14 GW) lead the national potential of about 102.18 GW.

s: The first national assessment titled “Solar PV Potential of India (Floating Solar)” was associated with which institution?
x: The first national assessment of floating solar PV potential was undertaken by the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE).

s: The Omkareshwar floating solar project (278 MW) is located on which river?
x: Omkareshwar floating solar is on the Narmada in Khandwa district, Madhya Pradesh, and is planned to reach 600 MW.

s: Where is Andhra Pradesh's floating solar plant located?
x: AP's floating plant is NTPC Simhadri (Visakhapatnam); Omkareshwar in MP is India's largest.

s: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of floating solar?
o: Lower upfront cost than land-based plants
x: Floating solar costs about 25% more upfront; saving land, cutting evaporation and better efficiency are its pluses.

s: How does the upfront cost of floating solar projects compare with that of land-based installations?
x: Floating solar costs about 25% more upfront, but saves land, reduces evaporation and gains efficiency from water cooling.

s: Which is India's largest floating solar project?
x: Omkareshwar floating solar (278 MW, to reach 600 MW) on the Narmada in Madhya Pradesh is India's largest floating solar project.
